subject: R_hat, effective sample size, ... are OK but divergent transitions

messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: R_hat, effective sample size, ... are OK but divergent transitions
parts:
Hi,

I have a concern. Suppose that in a case R_hat, effective sample size, MC errors, pen tests for the trace plots (that I often check when working with OpenBUGS and JAGS) are OK but we have a number of divergent transitions.

Does this mean in general that the model still have something wrong? And in this case are the parameter estimates reliable?

Would you have any idea?

Tran.

Thanks a lot!

Maybe I miss something, but from where you take the true value 0.7657852 'abline(h=0.7657852, col="grey", lty="dashed", lwd=3)' to compare with the sampled values of log(tau)?

Thank you for your time,

Tran.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R_hat, effective sample size, ... are OK but divergent transitions
parts:
The true value is shown to demonstrate that the diagnostics
indeed identify biased inferences.  It will indeed not be available
in a real analysis.

Also in a real analysis you will not know which trace plot might
exhibit pathological behavior.  You have to use the structure of
the specific model to motivate where to look.  But the point is
that divergences will identify problems for you so you don’t
have to go looking at all of the trace plots one by one.
On Mar 31, 2017, at 8:55 AM, Trung Dung Tran <trungd...@gmail.com> wrote:

In addition, in practice when estimating the parameters, we do not have true values to compare.

Tran.
